correctness.rationale: Analytic F-double-prime root bound implies at most three positive stationary points of throughput. Rational interval checks certify alternating derivative signs at four times for both endpoint fractions; affine dependence gives three and only three simple roots uniformly. Endpoint yield comparisons force opposite global winners. A >1/2 versus <1/2 envelope derivative separation forces a unique crossover. The attached reproducible checker passes 61 rigorously rational assertions and no numerical fit is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two separated, globally competing survey-duration designs emerge from a natural discrete-brightness source population with a two-photon detection threshold and overhead. A unique sharp composition crossover causes a large jump in optimal exposure, supplying a mathematical diagnostic against blindly assuming a unimodal dwell-time objective. The theorem establishes a uniform interval and structural derivative bounds, not an arbitrary isolated numerical instance; the gamma-density modality background and other known techniques are explicitly credited. No field-survey practical efficacy claimed.
